title: KV-windowed coalescer + safety playbook for continuous batching policy
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a production-ready, KV-aware coalescing/batching recommender with a documented safety playbook that can apply continuous parameter updates (coalescing window, min_batch_ms, kv_hit_threshold, per-model upper bounds) via staged rollout and automatic rollback.

Motivation: Many workloads show large per-token cost gains from increased coalescing and prefix-KV reuse, but naive apply of aggressive parameters has caused tail-latency regressions and occasional quality regressions when cross-model heuristics over-merge requests. This ticket ships a combined profiling + heuristic scoring pipeline and a conservative safe-apply plan with automatic rollback triggers and shadow-run validation to minimize customer risk while recovering cost.

Scope:
- Build a lightweight workload profiler that extracts: tokens/request distribution, request inter-arrival CDF, per-model KV hit-rate (observed), median and p95 generation latency, top prompt templates, and cross-model similarity scoring.
- Implement a heuristic scorer that suggests configuration tuples: {coalesce_window_ms, min_batch_samples, max_batch_tokens, kv_hit_threshold, per-model cap}. Each suggestion includes an estimated cost delta and confidence band.
- Add a shadow-apply pipeline to run proposed config in shadow for 0.1%–1% of traffic (configurable per-customer) and compare latency/throughput/quality to baseline.
- Design staged rollout: canary (0.1%), ramp (1% -> 25%), full (100%) with hold windows and comparison checks.
- Define rollback triggers: latency p95 > SLO + 150ms for sustained 3 consecutive windows; error rate increase > 2x baseline; quality regression on evaluation prompt-set (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim delta) beyond threshold; KV hit-rate decline > 10% causing cost inversion.
- Automation: ability to schedule automated apply attempts during low-traffic windows, auto-rollback on triggers, and generate a post-mortem summary to Slack and the rollout dashboard.

Non-goals: automatic model-level quantization changes, deep model re-ranking, or unsafe aggressive merges without shadow validation.

Implementation notes:
- Profiler runs as a streaming aggregation job that writes daily snapshots and a short-term 1-hour sliding window for rollouts. Use existing telemetry topic (inbound-telemetry.v2) and reuse tokenization utilities from runtime/core.
- Heuristic scoring uses a mixture of deterministic rules and a small gradient-boosted model trained on historical rollout outcomes (features: tokens_per_req_p50, interarrival_95ms_pct, kv_hit_rate, prompt-template-cluster, model_size). The model weights are stored in model-registry v2 and versioned with explainability metadata.
- Shadow-run enforces full parity on inputs (no sampling) and records KV hits/hits-after-coalescing to estimate theoretical cost-savings without affecting production outputs. Shadow results are stored in a protected S3 bucket and surfaced in the rollout dashboard for 72 hours.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Profiling pipeline produces per-model snapshots with required metrics for 95% of active models within 24 hours of deployment.
- Heuristic scorer outputs top-3 parameter tuples with cost delta and confidence metadata.
- Shadow-run pipeline completes end-to-end for a canary suggestion and reports latency/quality deltas in the rollout dashboard.
- Rollout automation can perform a staged apply and will auto-rollback if any trigger fires.
- Runbook and playbook docs exist and are linked in the ticket.

Risks / open questions:
- Measurement noise on low-volume customers: decide minimum traffic thresholds or synthetic traffic injection.
- Quality regression detection sensitivity: set initial thresholds conservatively and iterate.
- Storage and retention cost for shadow traces.

Next steps:
1) Wire profiler -> heuristic scorer (week 1)
2) Implement shadow-run plumbing + storage retention policy (week 2)
3) Build rollout orchestration + rollback circuit (week 3)
4) Internal canary with infra team -> gather metrics -> refine thresholds (week 4)
